I would keep it simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the safest and most familiar path for me is still the winter wheat and summer maize rotation, because it fits the local weather, the irrigation conditions, and the way I already know how to manage fields. I would not spread myself across too many crops. With my schooling and the need to control risk, I would rather plant the crops I understand well, use improved seed, fertilize enough for a stable yield, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide use limited to the times I really need it. I would carry the winter wheat through spring management and harvest it in early summer, then seed summer maize right after harvest so the land does not sit idle. For wheat, I would focus on topdressing nitrogen, watering at jointing and grain filling if moisture is short, and watching for aphids and disease. For maize, I would sow quickly after wheat harvest, use no-tillage or very light tillage to save time and moisture, push nitrogen mainly around the big bell stage, and control weeds and corn borers in time. That is the plan I would trust most for steady grain and steady cash this year.
